matthew.20.p1.b1.text: “For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.

matthew.20.p1.b2.text: He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day

matthew.20.p1.b3.text: and sent them into his vineyard.

matthew.20.p2.b1.text: About the third hour he went out and saw others standing in the marketplace doing nothing.

matthew.20.p2.b2.text: You also go into my vineyard, … and I will pay you whatever is right.

matthew.20.p2.b3.text: So they went. He went out again about the sixth hour and the ninth hour and did the same thing.

matthew.20.p3.b1.text: About the eleventh hour he went out and found still others standing around.

matthew.20.p3.b2.text: Why have you been standing here all day long doing nothing?

matthew.20.p3.b3.text: Because no one has hired us

matthew.20.p3.b4.text: You also go into my vineyard.

matthew.20.p4.b1.text: Call the workers and pay them their wages, starting with the last ones hired and moving on to the first.

matthew.20.p4.b2.text: The workers who were hired about the eleventh hour came and each received a denarius.

matthew.20.p4.b3.text: So when the original workers came, they assumed they would receive more.

matthew.20.p4.b4.text: But each of them also received a denarius.

matthew.20.p5.b1.text: On receiving their pay, they began to grumble against the landowner.

matthew.20.p5.b2.text: ‘These men who were hired last worked only one hour,’ they said, ‘and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden and the scorching heat of the day.’

matthew.20.p5.b3.text: Friend, I am not being unfair to you.

matthew.20.p5.b4.text: Did you not agree with me on one denarius?

matthew.20.p6.b1.text: Take your pay and go. I want to give this last man the same as I gave you.

matthew.20.p6.b2.text: … Or are you envious because I am generous?

matthew.20.p6.b3.text: So the last will be first, and the first will be last.”

matthew.20.p7.b1.text: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, He took the twelve disciples aside

matthew.20.p7.b2.text: Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes.

matthew.20.p7.b3.text: … and crucified. And on the third day He will be raised to life.

matthew.20.p8.b1.text: Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons and knelt down to make a request of Him.

matthew.20.p8.b3.text: Declare that in Your kingdom one of these two sons of mine may sit at Your right hand, and the other at Your left.

matthew.20.p9.b1.text: You do not know what you are asking, … Can you drink the cup I am going to drink?

matthew.20.p9.b3.text: You will indeed drink My cup, … But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom My Father has prepared them.

matthew.20.p10.b1.text: When the ten heard about this, they were indignant with the two brothers.

matthew.20.p10.b2.text: You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.

matthew.20.p10.b3.text: It shall not be this way among you. … whoever wants to be first among you must be your slave

matthew.20.p10.b4.text: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”

matthew.20.p11.b1.text: As they were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed Him.

matthew.20.p11.b2.text: Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!

matthew.20.p11.b3.text: The crowd admonished them to be silent,

matthew.20.p11.b4.text: Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!

matthew.20.p12.b2.text: What do you want Me to do for you?

matthew.20.p12.b3.text: Lord, … let our eyes be opened.

matthew.20.p13.b1.text: Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes,

matthew.20.p13.b2.text: and at once they received their sight
